title: Three Dollars to Ten
statement: You start with \$3 and repeatedly bet \$1 on fair coin flips. You stop when you reach \$0 or \$10. What is the probability you reach \$10?
insight: A fair game keeps your expected fortune constant, including at the stopping time, so 10·p = 3.
redHerring: Writing the 9 linear equations for each starting fortune and solving the system by hand.
hints: What is your expected fortune after one bet? After many bets?
When you stop, your fortune is either 0 or 10.
Set the expected final fortune equal to the starting fortune.
solution:
Each bet is fair, so your expected fortune never changes. The game stops in finite time with a bounded fortune, so the expected final fortune is still \$3 (optional stopping).

If $p$ is the chance of reaching \$10, the expected final fortune is $10p + 0(1-p) = 3$, so $p = \tfrac{3}{10}$.
